feedback: The candidate is not in the exact paper format. FINAL_STATES exists (u4) and is declared and accepting, but the machine is broken structurally and semantically: (1) u4 is never an absorbing/accepting terminal that can be reached cleanly — order_served goes u3→u4, but u4 then reopens on siren_ringing/client_arrived, making u4 effectively a u0 clone; that is acceptable for a recurring task, but here u4 is declared FINAL yet the agent can be in u4 during idle stretches, so FINAL is meaningless. (2) Critical task clause 'if the food falls, pick it up on your very next move' is not modeled anywhere: no state or transition tracks a food_fell and no reward penalizes a delayed pickup. (3) The siren subtask is mis-modeled: after serving (u3→u4) a ringing siren goes to u1 where a reward is paid only for switching it off; but in u3, siren_ringing self-loops earn nothing (reward function has no entry for u3 ringing self-loops or u2 ringing self-loops), so the shaping is sparse and inconsistent with 'whenever the siren rings, turn it off'. (4) Missing dense/progress structure: no per-step negative shaping for a client waiting while the siren rings (the environment's -0.5 pattern), and the 'progress reward is dense but bounded' requirement is only weakly met with ±0.1 tokens whose semantics are unclear. (5) Ordered-transition coverage gaps: order_taken while siren ringing is handled only via self-loop in u2, but order_taken can coincide with switch_toggled per the one-toggle-per-target constraint? No — that's fine — but food_prepared & client_arrived & order_served collisions and food_fell coinciding with other events are not disambiguated. (6) Reward entries reference transitions like (u3, food_prepared, u3) that give +0.1 for preparing, but no negative for serving late or letting the client wait; reward magnitudes are arbitrary and not tied to the env's +1/-0.5 schedule. (7) The else self-loops in u1 incorrectly latch: (u1, client_arrived) -> u1 keeps a client pending while in siren state, but then u1's else never returns to u2 if client arrived before siren was silenced AND then siren silenced — actually (u1, switch_toggled) -> u0 drops the pending client to u0, losing the client_arrived obligation (client goes untracked in u0; it will be re-triggered only if another client_arrived event occurs, but 'One client at a time' guarantees no new arrival before service — so the client's order/serve chain is permanently lost). This is a fatal reachability/coverage bug: a client arriving during a ring gets abandoned after the switch is toggled. Similar loss: (u3, switch_toggled) -> u3 is fine, but (u1, switch_toggled & client_arrived) -> u2 vs (u1, switch_toggled) -> u0 ordering means the conjunction takes priority, good — but the plain toggle still loses the client. (8) served_while_ringing proposition is unused despite being available, though not strictly required. Reject; redesign to (a) track the pending client across siren handling without dropping it, (b) add a food_fell→pickup-on-next-move tracking state with explicit reward, (c) penalize late service/late siren silencing densely and boundedly, and (d) make FINAL_STATES meaningful or absorb recurring-task reentry through u0 rather than through a fake terminal u4.

feedback: The candidate conflates the three independent task clauses into one sequential machine and, in doing so, rewards the wrong behaviours and misses required ones. (1) Structure/fidelity: the siren duty (turn it off whenever it rings) and the client duty (order -> prepare -> serve) are orthogonal and can overlap in any combination — e.g. the siren rings while a client is being served, or a client arrives before the siren is silenced. A single state graph that pushes food_fell to a dedicated u4 (which erases siren/client context) and jumps to u0 on switch_toggled cannot represent these interleavings faithfully; ordered-transition coverage for the true task is not achieved. (2) The fall clause ('pick it up on your very next move') requires checking holding_food at the step immediately after food_fell; the machine only enters u4 on food_fell and immediately leaves it via else-self-loops on any event, never tracking whether the pickup happened on the next step, so this clause is not enforced or rewarded. (3) food_fell transitions are listed after the main per-state rules, so in states where e.g. (u2, switch_toggled) matches, ordered-transition semantics may shadow the fall handling depending on the evaluation order — the ordering is unsafe and should be made explicit or the guards disjoint. (4) Reward shape: order_served gives 1.0 in every state, but food_prepared and order_taken give 0.1 only from specific states (u1, u4), so the pipeline order/prepare/serve is only partially credited and is silent in other states; progress rewards are not dense across the machine and are not aligned with the task decomposition. (5) served_while_ringing, holding_food, and switch_toggled-while-silent (a toggle with no ring up) are unused; the else-self-loops do not cover irrelevant events per-state for states like u5/u6 which lack food_fell priority, and several event/precondition distinctions (e.g. siren_ringing as condition vs. its onset) are ignored. (6) Persistent/event distinction: siren_ringing is used as a transition trigger every step while it persists, which double-counts states; switch_toggled is a one-step event and its pairing with siren_ringing conditions in the same label is not disambiguated (both can hold simultaneously, e.g. toggle that silences a ringing siren). A faithful machine should track (siren on/off, client-waiting substate, food-carry substate, fall-pending flag) as orthogonal components — e.g. a product machine — with the fall clause implemented as a one-step pending deadline requiring holding_food on the next step, and rewards assigned for closing each clause exactly once per occurrence, not as a flat 1.0 for order_served regardless of context.
